correctness.rationale: PASS: Completed the Gaussian square and recovered the exponential profile coefficient identity, including identification of both carrier magnitude coefficients and nu (one-zero-amplitude cases are treated separately). Cross term at three observation times is a real 3×2 matrix with unit rows and angles 0,−πt,−πrho*t, hence Gram eigenvalues (3±|Σ exp(2i angles)|)/2. Zero requires t and rho*t integers; rho irrational forbids positive resonance. Using 9−|S|²=4[sin²πt+sin²πrho*t+sin²π(rho−1)t], elementary sine bounds yield (4/3)(||t||²+||rho*t||²)≤lambda≤2π²(||t||²+||rho*t||²). Nearest integers q≈t,p≈rho*t show the lower exponent via irrationality definition; convergent denominators t=q achieve the matching limsup, including infinite exponent for Liouville rho. Exact Gabor profile reduction and 3×2 Gram were independently checked; grid tests for four rho values corroborate uniform comparison but do not establish the asymptotic theorem.

value.rationale: PASS: The exact conditioning of a naturally minimal three-line phase design is governed by the classical Diophantine irrationality exponent, distinguishing injectivity from arbitrarily poor high-frequency robustness. The natural invariant is the smallest singular value of the *extracted interference moment*, and the precise exponent is useful for choosing irrational sensor spacings; it is not misrepresented as raw spectrogram stability.

final_claim: For symmetric two-tone Gaussian signals from full STFT frequency profiles at x=0,d,rho*d, rho>1, the extracted three-phase interference matrix A has squared least singular value (3−|1+exp(2πit)+exp(2πi rho t)|)/2, t=2nu*d. For irrational rho this is positive at all finite t>0 and satisfies limsup_{t→∞}[-log lambda_rho(t)]/log t=2(mu(rho)−1), with sharp polynomial badly-approximable and Liouville contrasts. The qualitative uniqueness of three irrationally spaced lines is prior work.
limitations: No claim to original qualitative irrational three-line uniqueness.
